title: Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphoning
description: When a fixture gurgles or smells like sewer gas, the issue often stems from poor ventilation rather than a clogged drain line. Drainage requires air movement to balance negative pressure as water flows. If a roof vent or air admittance valve becomes blocked, moving wastewater pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This siphoning breaks the water seal, allowing sewer gases to enter the building. Inspecting vent terminals for debris, bird nests, or frost closures, and testing secondary air admittance valves, can pinpoint air intake restrictions without needlessly snaking clear drain lines.

Troubleshooting Gurgling Drains and Trap Siphoning

When a fixture gurgles or smells like sewer gas, the issue often stems from poor ventilation rather than a clogged drain line. Drainage requires air movement to balance negative pressure as water flows. If a roof vent or air admittance valve becomes blocked, moving wastewater pulls water out of nearby P-traps. This siphoning breaks the water seal, allowing sewer gases to enter the building. Inspecting vent terminals for debris, bird nests, or frost closures, and testing secondary air admittance valves, can pinpoint air intake restrictions without needlessly snaking clear drain lines.
